name: fOXX / Ridinger Associates Inc.
notes: TONEHOME documents the fOXX Clean Machine as made by Ridinger Associates Inc. in Chatsworth, California, in the early 1970s. This is an important family-tree-independent manufacturer discovery because the product is documented from a 1970s period context rather than through a famous-circuit related-model tree.

name: EKO
notes: TONEHOME documents the EKO Multitone as made in Italy in the early 1970s and cites a 1973 EKO catalog. The Multitone combines wah, distortion, booster, repeat percussion and volume functions, making EKO a strong independent historical effects node.

name: Jennings Electronic Industries (JEI)
notes: Fuzzboxes documents JEI's pedal-control and rotary fuzz products, with the effects series in production from 1968 and a limited treadle-style Fuzz surviving as a rare physical example. Preserve JEI as a manufacturer/brand node separate from later relationships.

name: Morley / Tel-Ray Electronics
notes: Morley traces its effects lineage to Tel-Ray Electronics and documents the Power Wah Fuzz as a 1970s Morley product. The PWF is valuable as a distinctive historical product lineage and as evidence that original-effects discovery must extend beyond classic fuzz-family trees.
